experiment.claim: spec/topology-survey.md Startup row ("self-starting, < 1 ms") -- the no-other-stable-state half. Substantiates that design/bandgap_core.sch + design/startup_injector.sch has exactly ONE DC operating point over the whole 0..VDD range of its startup node GDRV, that the zero-current state the bare core does have (reproduced here as the control instance) is actively driven away from by microamps rather than merely being unlikely, and that the loop is pulled downhill by a bounded-below current everywhere in the degenerate region rather than merely somewhere in it. Also bounds what attaching the injector costs the running circuit: the residual current it draws out of GDRV and the shift that puts on the reference. The startup TIME claim is the sibling experiment sim/startup-ramp/; the +/-1% output-accuracy claim is issue #11.
experiment.statistical_convention: N/A (corner-matrix claim, not a distribution claim)
experiment.title: Startup: the degenerate zero-current state is not an operating point once the injector is attached

matrix.subset_reason: Issue #10's stated worst-corner matrix for this experiment: slow/fast process (ss/ff) plus tt as the nominal reference, temperature endpoints -40/125 degC, supply endpoints 2.97/3.63 V. The 27 degC row and the sf/fs skew corners are dropped because the mechanisms this experiment bounds -- the injector's release threshold against the core's self-sustaining point, the disengaged reference's residual current, and (new in issue #52) MNC's VOUT-vs-GDRV ordering test -- are all monotone in the dropped axes, so an interior point cannot be worse than both endpoints. This is the same 12-corner matrix every prior record of this experiment ran, repeated unchanged so this record is directly comparable with 20260803-124600-e599e30 (pre-issue-#41 amp) and with the single-corner regression records 20260803-144531-544cc5e / 20260803-144658-4226657 it supersedes.

spread_checks.note: The startup node's operating voltage tracks the supply (GDRV ~ VDD - |Vgs_p|), so a full-matrix run must show it moving by more than the +/-10 % supply span. A flat vgdrv_dut across the matrix means the corner/supply knobs are not reaching the simulator.
Untrimmed output over process and temperature must move by more than 10 mV; a frozen value would indicate the .lib corner or .temp injection stopped taking effect.
